title: Build a hand detector with an IR sensor
safety: Unplug the USB cable before changing any wire.
Power the sensor from the 3.3V pin, not 5V: the UNO Q pins use 3.3V logic.
Never connect 3.3V or 5V directly to GND.
Never connect the board's 5V pin to a signal pin.
materials: Joy-IT SEN-KY032IR infrared obstacle sensor (pins: EN, OUT/Signal, +V, GND; green EN jumper fitted)

steps.title: Identify the parts
steps.goal: Learner identifies the UNO Q, the KY-032 IR sensor, the breadboard and the jumper wires, and finds the sensor's +V, GND and signal pins.
steps.intro_display: Find the board, IR sensor and breadboard.
steps.intro_spoken: Let's build a hand detector. Put the Arduino, the infrared sensor and the breadboard in front of you and take a photo.
steps.visual_success_criteria: An Arduino board, a small sensor board with an IR LED and IR receiver (KY-032 / SEN-KY032IR), a breadboard and jumper wires are visible.
hint_levels: The sensor is the small black board with pins.
Read the tiny labels next to the sensor's pins.
Look for GND, +V and OUT (signal) on the sensor.
steps.check_question: Which three sensor pins do we need?

steps.title: Power, ground, signal
steps.goal: Learner explains that the sensor needs power (+V), ground (GND) and a signal wire, and that the signal changes when something is in front of it.
steps.intro_display: Why does the sensor need three wires?
steps.intro_spoken: Before wiring: why does the sensor need three wires and not just one?
hint_levels: The sensor needs energy to work. Where from?
Energy needs a way in and a way back.
Plus and GND power it; the third wire reports.
steps.check_question: What does each of the three wires do?

steps.title: Power the sensor
steps.goal: Sensor sits in the breadboard; +V row wired to the UNO Q 3.3V pin, GND row to a GND pin. With USB connected, the sensor's own LED lights up when a hand is close.
steps.intro_display: Wire +V to 3.3V and GND to GND.
steps.intro_spoken: Unplug the USB cable. Put the sensor into the breadboard, then connect its plus pin to 3.3 volts and its ground pin to GND. Take a photo when you are done.
steps.visual_success_criteria: Sensor plugged into the breadboard; one wire from the sensor's +V row to the board's 3.3V header pin and one from the GND row to a GND header pin. No wire between 3.3V/5V and GND directly.
hint_levels: Male wires can't go into the sensor pins directly.
Plug the sensor into the breadboard first.
Red: +V row to 3.3V. Black: GND row to GND.
steps.check_question: Hold your hand close. Does the sensor LED light?

steps.title: Read the signal
steps.goal: Signal (OUT) row wired to digital pin D2; the sketch from hardware/ir_hand_detector is uploaded; the board's LED turns on when a hand is close.
steps.intro_display: Connect OUT to pin D2, upload the sketch.
steps.intro_spoken: Now connect the sensor's OUT pin to digital pin 2 and upload the hand detector sketch. Then test it with your hand.
steps.visual_success_criteria: A third wire runs from the sensor's OUT/signal row to header pin D2 (digital 2).
hint_levels: The sketch reads pin 2. Where must OUT go?
Digital pins are on the header labelled D0-D13.
steps.check_question: Does the board LED react to your hand?

steps.title: Find the bug
steps.goal: A partner moves the signal wire from D2 to D3 (the sketch still reads D2). Learner finds that the code and the wiring disagree and fixes it.
steps.intro_display: I changed something. Find the bug!
steps.intro_spoken: Ask your partner to move one wire while you look away. Then find out why the board no longer reacts, even though the sensor LED still lights.
steps.visual_success_criteria: The signal wire is visible and on pin D2 again after the fix.
hint_levels: The sensor LED still works. So power is fine.
Which pin does the sketch read? Which one is wired?
The signal wire must go to D2, like in the code.
steps.check_question: Why did the board stop reacting?

steps.title: Explain it back
steps.goal: Learner explains the full chain: IR light reflects off the hand, the sensor pulls OUT LOW (active low), the board reads D2 and switches its LED.
steps.intro_spoken: Last step. In your own words: what happens from your hand to the light on the board?
hint_levels: Start with the light the sensor sends out.
What happens to the OUT signal near a hand?
Reflection, OUT goes LOW, board reads D2, LED on.
steps.check_question: How does your hand turn the LED on?
